items.title: Crunchbase Data Shows Q3 Robotics Startup Funding Jumps 185% As US And China Lead Physical AI Push
items.summary: Venture funding to robotics startups has soared in 2026, with the bulk of investment going to companies based in China and the U.S., Crunchbase data shows. All told, global venture funding to robotics startups totaled $9.9 billion in Q3, more than double the $4.3 billion invested in Q3 2025, per Crunchbase data.

items.title: Your AI Agents Need A Chief Operating Officer, Too
items.summary: Scaling AI agents requires treating them like employees in regulated roles, with written rules, clearly defined responsibilities and a named human manager accountable for their performance. Guest author Rick Folgmann, COO at Get Covered, tells companies they should start with tasks governed by established rules, adjust autonomy to each workflow’s risks, and regularly review results before expanding agents’ authority.

items.title: Some Observations About Anthropic’s IPO Filing
items.summary: In an S-1 filing today preceding what could be the largest IPO ever, Anthropic laid out extensive new details about its earnings, growth, key stakeholders and the risks it faces going forward. Clocking in at 335 pages, the document wasn’t exactly light reading. However, in a preliminary once-over, we highlight some of the more intriguing disclosures.

items.title: When Traction Becomes Personal Exposure: What The Joonko Guilty Plea Means For Founders
items.summary: False claims about customers, revenue and AI capabilities can expose founders to personal securities-fraud liability, with D&O insurance offering limited protection against established misconduct. Guest author Kyle Jeziorski of Founder Shield shares three policy provisions that need close attention from founders.

items.title: California Startups Have Raised More So Far In 2026 Than The Entire US Ever Has In A Single Year

items.title: The Week’s 10 Biggest Funding Rounds: AI Drives A Varied Lineup Of Large Financings
items.summary: It was another interesting week for AI-related startup funding, with a number of large rounds and quirky companies. The largest financings went to Tenstorrent, a developer of AI processors and systems, and AI lab Flapping Airplanes. The quirkiest round, meanwhile, was undoubtedly a $200 million financing for Warhound, which wants to breed elite military dogs. A number of big rounds in areas including biotech, space tech and physical AI rounded out the list.

items.title: Protecting Trade Secrets In The Age Of AI
items.summary: AI agents create new trade secret risks by allowing employees to access expertise or inadvertently expose proprietary information through personal devices. In this guest commentary, Seth Kugler, a partner at Grellas Shah LLP, warns companies that they should adopt strict AI policies, restrict data access on unmanaged devices, update confidentiality agreements, and act immediately when misuse is suspected.

items.title: 5 Interesting Startup Deals You May Have Missed: Robot Training, Space Lasers And Greener Cement

items.title: The AI IPO Wave Is The Dot-Com Bubble’s Evil Twin. Anthropic’s Delay Just Proved It.
items.summary: In this guest article from Airrived co-founder and CEO Anurag Gurtu, he contends that Anthropic’s rapid revenue growth does not justify its proposed $2 trillion IPO valuation, given enormous infrastructure commitments, safety concerns, customer concentration and competition from cheaper open-weight models, saying instead that lasting enterprise AI value will come from proprietary data, reliable deployment and measurable customer outcomes rather than expensive models alone.
